newsitem.title: USA: United Financial Group files Chapter 11.
newsitem.headline: United Financial Group files Chapter 11.

text.p: United Financial Group Inc Tuesday filed for Chapter 11 protection in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware, court papers say.
The company listed assets of $11.7 million and liabilities of $17.5 million, almost all of it in fixed liquidated unsecured debt with 2,900 holders.
According to court papers, the bankruptcy petition was accompanied by a reorganization plan under which the company hopes to emerge from Chapter 11 protection.

Maxxam Inc owns 17.4 percent of the common stock of the company and 93.5 percent of the Series E preferred stock; Maxxam's affiliate, MCO Properties Inc, owns 9.8 percent of the common stock and 6.5 percent of the Series E preferred stock; and Nu-West Florida Inc owns 100 percent of the Series B preferred stock, court papers say.
United Financial is a Houston-based company that manages short-term investments pending settlement of claims.
Prior to December 30, 1988, the company was a savings and loan holding firm which owned all the stock of United Savings Association of Texas, a chartered savings and loan company.
According to published reports, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp (FDIC) sued Charles Hurwitz, who owns 31 percent of Maxxam, alleging he allowed the savings and loan to fail in 1988.
United Financial owns 100 percent of the voting securities of PLC Stock Holdings Inc, Group Investors Trust Co, PennCorp Financial Inc and United Savings Association of Texas, court papers say.

Among the 20 largest unsecured creditors are First Trust of California N.A. of Los Angeles, the indenture trustee for $4.7 million in a nine percent secured sinking fund debentures due 1993; and the FDIC with $11 million dollars in maintenance claims related to a 1995 settlement agreement.
